## Methods and limitations

- **Attention, not value.** Wikipedia pageviews are a proxy for public
  attention. They are not a measure of sponsorship value, reach or return.
- **Baseline.** A day's lift compares its views with the average of the 28
  days before it (the day itself is excluded). Days the API reports no views
  count as zero.
- **Medians, not averages,** summarise match-day lift, so one viral day
  doesn't dominate a club's number.
- **Match day** is the UTC day that holds the match: the UTC date two hours
  after kickoff, on the same clock Wikimedia uses. A 7:30 pm ET kickoff
  (23:30 UTC) counts on the next UTC day, when the match and the evening
  after it happen. An earlier version used the UTC date of kickoff, which
  measured about a third of club-matches on the day before they were played.
- **Sponsor attention on match day** compares each match day with the same
  brand's non-match days on the same weekday, during the deal only (an as-of
  join on the deal's start and end). A sign test per brand checks whether more
  match days sit above that norm than chance would give, with a
  Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment because every brand is tested at once.
- **Results** are from each club's own point of view. A pageview day includes
  the hours before kickoff, so result comparisons show correlation, not cause.
- **Year over year** compares the same calendar window (January 1 to the
  latest day of data) in each year.
- **Deal dates** are recorded by season. A deal runs from 1 January of its
  first season to 31 December of its last, unless an exact date is known.
  Most rows are `first_observed` (the first season we have a source for), so
  the dataset is a reliable picture of 2026, not yet a full history.
- **Who sold it.** Stadium rows record whether the club or an outside venue
  owner sold the name. Kit assets are always sold by the club.
- **Reported values** are shown only when a published source reports them,
  and are labelled "reported".
- **Coverage.** The dataset is maintained by hand and may miss recent changes.
  Each row links to its source and the date it was checked. Open questions
  are listed in
  [`data/TO_VERIFY.md`](https://github.com/chrisantosiewicz/MLS-partnership-tracker/blob/main/data/TO_VERIFY.md).

## Pipeline

Every morning a GitHub Actions job fetches new pageviews and match results,
rebuilds a DuckDB warehouse from scratch, runs every SQL data test, and only
then renders and publishes this site. If a test fails, nothing is published and
yesterday's site stays up. The data model is documented in
[`docs/DATA_MODEL.md`](https://github.com/chrisantosiewicz/MLS-partnership-tracker/blob/main/docs/DATA_MODEL.md).

## Sources

- **Sponsorship data:** compiled by Chris Antosiewicz from club and brand
  announcements and press coverage. Each row's source is in the
  [dataset](https://github.com/chrisantosiewicz/MLS-partnership-tracker/blob/main/data/partnerships.csv).
  Licensed CC BY 4.0.
- **Pageviews:** [Wikimedia Analytics API](https://doc.wikimedia.org/generated-data-platform/aqs/analytics-api/) (CC0).
- **Match schedules and results:** [American Soccer Analysis](https://www.americansocceranalysis.com/).
